This is the first screen of the journey that today only exists as an eleven-minute phone call (seq 3, seq 4).

Propose the next screen.

The result sits inline; the no-match decision — continue anyway or go back — is the one question this screen asks, so it is the modal.

text:
Filed **confirmation-of-payee-result**. The base screen holds the inline result (a `list-row` inside a `card`, carrying the match label, the computed result, and the warn tone — the fact the agent currently narrates) and a `modal-dialog`, hidden in the ideal/match state and revealed only when the result is a no-match, which is the one real decision this screen asks. A close-match or ok result needs no modal at all — the same parts, different visibility, per the state convention.

Note: the Verdant-scenario `status-chip` part (enum `ok|due|overdue`) doesn't fit this domain's match semantics, so I used `list-row.tone` instead to carry the warn/critical signal — naming this here since it's a vocabulary fit decision, not a gap.

Awaiting your decision. The next candidates are the scam-intervention/warning screen for a coached customer (seq 6, seq 8, seq 30) or the account-to-pay-from balance check before first payment (seq 6's one-in-twenty retry).
